learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the principles governing the vibratory motion of mechanical systems.
Knowledge of dynamic modeling of mechanical systems.
Knowledge of analysis of mathematical models of vibrating mechanical systems.
Knowledge in determining the natural frequencies of mechanical systems.
Knowledge of the physical quantities used in the Mechanical Vibrations discipline and their units of measurement.
Ability to understand the physical phenomena that lead to the appearance of vibrations in mechanical systems.
Ability to solve vibration problems; to determine the natural frequency/natural frequencies for mechanical systems with one/multiple degrees of freedom.
Acquire experimental skills in measuring physical quantities used in the study of vibrations.
Create subroutines in computer programs that allow the calculation of natural frequencies of bodies/mechanical systems.

syllabus_topics: Elements of vibration kinematics: Harmonic vibrations.
Vectorial representation of harmonic vibrations.
Complex representation of harmonic vibrations.
Composition of harmonic vibrations: collinear synchronous, collinear of different frequencies, orthogonal of the same frequency.
Fourier analysis of a non-harmonic periodic vibration.
Vibrations of mechanical systems with one degree of freedom.
Free undamped vibrations.
Free damped vibrations.
Forced undamped vibrations.
Forced damped vibrations produced by harmonic disturbing forces.
Vibrations of mechanical systems with two degrees of freedom.
Influence coefficient method.
Free vibrations.
Vibrations of mechanical systems with multiple degrees of freedom.
Derivation of differential equations using Lagrange's equation.
Translation model.
Rotation model.
Free undamped vibrations.
Modal coordinates.
Problems of vectorial representation of harmonic vibrations.
Vibrations of mechanical systems with one degree of freedom.
Vibrations of mechanical systems with 2 degrees of freedom.
Study of the diagram of a damped vibration.
Composition of harmonic vibrations.
Fourier transform of a non-harmonic periodic function.
Simple dynamic damper.
Determination of critical speeds for a shaft with a rotor.
Determination of natural frequencies of a mechanical system with 3 degrees of freedom.
assessment_rules: Minimum performance requires 70% attendance at courses and seminars, 100% attendance at laboratories, and fulfillment of all laboratory tasks. Students must achieve a minimum grade of 5 for seminar verification assignments and a minimum grade of 5 on each of the four exam topics. The written exam covers theory, demonstrations, and problems for one and two-degree-of-freedom mechanical systems.
